contracts.boundary: local fail-closed controller verifies an independent receipt, exact candidate/proposed-merge evidence, GitHub checks, review state, and post-merge push evidence before recording outcome; immediately before merge it re-fetches the proposed merge SHA, tree, and ordered parents and requires them to remain the originally bound identity with parents exactly [base, head]; check rereads the canonical receipt after GitHub checks and reads artifact ZIPs with Python 3 isolated imports. After the final GitHub reads, it repeats canonical receipt path, digest, shape, expected identity, and evidence binding before persisting apply intent. Apply requires a live active repository ruleset with strict release-gates checks, pull-request enforcement and no bypass actors; this server policy closes the base-movement window after local reads.
contracts.assertions: Controller never invokes merge when required evidence is stale, unavailable, altered, unresolved, or the final proposed merge identity moves; check never records merged-and-verified if the receipt is revoked during its GitHub checks; a shadow zipfile.py in the launch directory cannot execute; dry run stays non-mutating and checks preserve frozen intent. Receipt revocation on the third PR read rejects with nonzero status, zero merge calls, and no apply intent. The third read must retain eligibility and the same workflow/run/attempt. Missing or bypassable strict server protection rejects; rejected dry runs preserve existing intent bytes. Atomic no-replace output publication also preserves an intent created concurrently during GitHub reads, for eligible and blocked dry runs. All fake-GitHub controller launchers use one fixture environment; the real concurrent-apply case pins an unrelated ambient GITHUB_REPOSITORY and still merges exactly once in its fixture.

boundaryTest.name: valid apply merges exactly once and verifies push gates

invariant.name: repeated apply preserves the frozen intent and never merges twice

fault.name: third PR read receipt revocation rejects before intent or merge

contracts.boundary: eligibility CLI re-fetches PR head/base and re-reads proposed-merge sha/parents/tree before returning an eligible result, bounds run, job, and review-thread evidence to one explicit first-100 page or fixed page/count/time bounds, and prints only fixed bounded terminal diagnostics.
contracts.assertions: Eligibility fails closed with fixed blockers when head or base moves, the proposed tree or parents change, inventories truncate, or pagination exceeds its bounds; untrusted PR body and GitHub response text never reaches stdout or stderr.

boundaryTest.name: CLI re-fetches head, base, and proposed identity before returning eligible

invariant.name: terminal control PR-body text never reaches terminal diagnostics

fault.name: guard removal control: disabling final revalidation reddens the movement assertion, restore is green

contracts.boundary: acceptance change evidence binds an event-driven push to the actual predecessor commit, keeps pull-request metadata authoritative, and fails closed without an environment-base fallback; the workflow acceptance CLI computes the case from installed dependencies on the real candidate. The sanitized unit gate forwards only the GitHub event name and payload path, preserving the real push predecessor without forwarding credentials.
contracts.assertions: Push events use event.before and reject missing, null, zero, stale, unknown, or intermediate bases; PR events use pull_request.base.sha despite a competing environment base; declaration base equality and changed-file coverage remain exact; the real acceptance CLI records GREEN for the actual merge predecessor and runs the named rejection and HEAD-parent fault controls. Removing event context from the actual gate environment fails the same named predecessor assertion on a checkout whose origin/v2 already equals HEAD.

boundaryTest.name: multi-commit push validates full event.before diff and rejects intermediate base

invariant.name: event-driven push and pull request bases fail closed despite competing env

fault.name: fault control: selecting HEAD parent instead of event.before turns push base RED

contracts.assertions: Hard group cancellation and direct owner SIGTERM leave neither owner group nor provider alive; the detached pre-fix launcher fails the identical named ownership assertion; uncertain cleanup retains scratch and preserves any pending error. Observed owner close does not imply immediate group reaping; a bounded absence wait is required before scratch reclamation.
